cases.quote: A.9 Iteration marks (cl-09) / 繰返し記号（cl-09）, first table row: ヽ | 30FD | KATAKANA ITERATION MARK | 片仮名繰返し記号 | [Remarks cell empty]. § 3.9.2 lists the same class: Iteration marks (cl-09) / 繰返し記号（cl-09）, illustrated ヽヾゝゞ々 etc. / ヽヾゝゞ々 など
cases.rationale: The first member of A.9's table, keyed on one code point. Every Remarks cell of A.9 is empty in both renderings, so nothing qualifies membership: there is no frame (字幅) fact, no writing-direction fact and no role fact for any of the six members. The item therefore declares no frame — cl-09 is not one of the five classes § 3.1.2 states a half-width advance for, so a declared frame would decide nothing here and stating one would put a fact in the input that the specification does not state. The rule cited is § 3.9.2, which is where the thirty classes are named; A.9 is a table rather than a statement and the rule inventory carries no address beginning `A.`.

cases.quote: A.9 Iteration marks (cl-09) / 繰返し記号（cl-09）, second table row: ヾ | 30FE | KATAKANA VOICED ITERATION MARK | 片仮名繰返し記号（濁点） | [Remarks cell empty]
cases.rationale: The voiced katakana mark is one code point in A.9, not the unvoiced mark followed by a voicing mark: the table keys it on U+30FE alone, and U+309B KATAKANA-HIRAGANA VOICED SOUND MARK appears nowhere in the published document, so no ordered-pair key of Appendix A can be built from it. An implementation that normalizes the input before looking a key up, or that composes a voiced mark out of two occurrences, answers this case with two items where the specification has one.

cases.quote: A.9 Iteration marks (cl-09) / 繰返し記号（cl-09）, third table row: ゝ | 309D | HIRAGANA ITERATION MARK | 平仮名繰返し記号 | [Remarks cell empty]
cases.rationale: The hiragana iteration mark. A.9 draws no distinction between its katakana and hiragana members: both scripts' marks are one class, and the class is not a function of the script of the character the mark repeats. Nothing in A.9's Remarks column separates them, and § 3.9.2 illustrates the class with both.

cases.quote: A.9 Iteration marks (cl-09) / 繰返し記号（cl-09）, fourth table row: ゞ | 309E | HIRAGANA VOICED ITERATION MARK | 平仮名繰返し記号（濁点） | [Remarks cell empty]
cases.rationale: The fourth member, and the second of the two voiced marks. Recorded for the same reason as U+30FE: it is one Appendix A key on one code point, and the specification lists no decomposed spelling of it anywhere.

cases.quote: A.9 Iteration marks (cl-09) / 繰返し記号（cl-09）, sixth and last table row: 〻 | 303B | VERTICAL IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK | 二の字点，ゆすり点 | [Remarks cell empty]. Contrast A.8: 〵 | 3035 | VERTICAL KANA REPEAT MARK LOWER HALF | くの字点下 | used in vertical composition / 縦組で使用
cases.rationale: The last member of A.9's table, in horizontal writing. Its UCS name begins VERTICAL and its Remarks cell is nevertheless empty in both renderings, while three keys in the neighboring A.8 carry `used in vertical composition` / `縦組で使用` in exactly that cell. The empty cell is therefore a statement and not an omission: JLReq restricts no member of cl-09 to one writing mode, and an implementation that reads the UCS name instead of the Remarks column refuses or reclassifies this occurrence. This case and its vertical twin declare the two directions and expect the same class, so the answer cannot be direction-conditional in either direction. § 3.9.2 also illustrates the class as ヽヾゝゞ々 etc. / ヽヾゝゞ々 など, which does not show U+303B; the illustration carries `etc.` and is not an enumeration, so it does not narrow A.9's six rows.

cases.quote: A.9 Iteration marks (cl-09) / 繰返し記号（cl-09）, sixth and last table row: 〻 | 303B | VERTICAL IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK | 二の字点，ゆすり点 | [Remarks cell empty]. Contrast A.8: 〵 | 3035 | VERTICAL KANA REPEAT MARK LOWER HALF | くの字点下 | used in vertical composition / 縦組で使用
cases.rationale: The same occurrence in vertical writing, with an expectation identical to its horizontal twin. The pair is the whole assertion: A.9 states no writing-mode qualification on any of its six members, so the class of U+303B is the same in both modes and no implementation may make membership conditional on the direction. Written as two direction-declaring cases rather than one direction-free case because the claim is about both modes rather than about neither.

cases.quote: (1) Very loose (Newspapers) / レベル1（新聞など）: Breaking a line is allowed before or after the following character classes even though Table 2 prohibits it. — Hyphens (cl-03); Dividing punctuation marks (cl-04); Middle dots (cl-05); Inseparable characters (cl-08) of the same kind; Iteration marks (cl-09); Prolonged sound mark (cl-10); Small kana (cl-11); Prefixed abbreviations (cl-12); Postfixed abbreviations (cl-13). — (2) Loose (Magazines) / レベル2（雑誌など）: … IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK "々" / 繰返し記号（cl-09）の繰返し記号[々] (IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK). — (3) Strict (Default, general publications) / レベル3（デフォルト，一般の書籍）: IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK "々"; Prolonged sound mark (cl-10); Small kana (cl-11).
cases.rationale: § C.3's level 1 relaxes iteration marks (cl-09) as a whole class, while levels 2 and 3 relax the single member IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK 々 — the Japanese rendering makes the granularity visible by naming it 繰返し記号（cl-09）の繰返し記号[々] where the English gives the bare character. That difference is about which occurrences may begin a line; it is not a change of class. Every level of § C.3 is stated as an override of Table 2 — `Breaking a line is allowed … even though Table 2 prohibits it` — and the only sentences in the document that move an iteration mark into another class are § C.2 note 1 and § E.2 note 1, which name 々 and nothing else. So no level and no reading of the relaxation mechanism makes KATAKANA ITERATION MARK a member of any class but cl-09, and the three entries below record that the answer is the same under all of them. An implementation that relaxes cl-09 at level 1 by reclassifying the class into cl-19 passes at that level for the wrong reason and is wrong at levels 2 and 3, where five of the six members are not relaxed at all.

permitted.source: § C.3 level 1 (Very loose, newspapers), which relaxes the class
§ C.3 level 1 read through the § C.2 notes, none of which names this member

forbidden.why: § C.2 note 1 and § E.2 note 1 state the move into ideographic characters (cl-19) for IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK "々" alone, and § C.3 states its levels as overrides of Table 2 rather than as changes of class. Nothing anywhere makes KATAKANA ITERATION MARK a member of cl-19.

cases.quote: In principle iteration marks (cl-09) should be placed neither at the line head nor at the head of an inline cutting note. When it happens with IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK "々", there are three ways to deal with this situation. (1) Follow the principle by applying some sort of line adjustment. In this case, IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK "々" remains in iteration marks (cl-09). (2) Allow IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK "々" to be placed either at the line head or at the head of an inline cutting note. In this case, the character shall be treated as part of the ideographic characters (cl-19) class. (3) Replace IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK "々" with the corresponding character. / 行頭又は割注行頭に繰返し記号（cl-09）を配置することは原則として禁止である．ただし，繰返し記号（cl-09）のうち，行頭に配置される繰返し記号[々] (IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK)については，次の3つの処理方法がある． — § C.2 note 1: If IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK "々" is allowed to appear at the line head or that of inline cutting note, the character shall be treated as a member of the ideographic character (cl-19) class. (For how it behaves in combination with other character classes, see the cells for ideographic characters (cl-19).)
cases.rationale: The one member of cl-09 whose class an implementation may legitimately answer two ways, and the reason the answer is a classification answer rather than a line-breaking one. § C.2 note 1 does not merely permit a break: it says the character `shall be treated as a member of` cl-19 and then sends the reader to cl-19's cells `for how it behaves in combination with other character classes`, and § E.2 note 1 repeats the sentence verbatim for the expansion tables. The reclassification is therefore total, so a relaxed 々 answers cl-19 to this question anywhere in the stream and not only where a line begins — which is why this case's input declares no line at all. The three overlays are § B.2 note 14's three methods. Under the third the mark is replaced only where it would be placed at a line head or a warichu (割注, inline cutting note) head; this occurrence is at neither, so its text is unchanged and its class is A.9's. What the third method does at a line head is a mutation of the input string, and its outcome cannot be stated as an expectation over these items — see the report accompanying this file. The English of the third method says only `the corresponding character` where the Japanese says 元の漢字, the original kanji; both worked examples (国 + 々 → 国 + 国, 人 + 々 → 人 + 人) resolve it in the Japanese direction, so the English is narrower rather than contradictory and no reading of it changes the class recorded here.

permitted.source: JLReq preferred (§ B.2 note 14, first method): the mark remains in cl-09
§ B.2 note 14, first method: IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK "々" remains in iteration marks (cl-09)
§ B.2 note 14, second method; § C.2 note 1 and § E.2 note 1: treated as a member of ideographic characters (cl-19)
§ B.2 note 14, third method, which changes only an occurrence placed at a line head or a warichu head

disagreements.behavior: Breaks before the six iteration marks 々 U+3005, 〻 U+303B, ゝ U+309D, ゞ U+309E, ヽ U+30FD and ヾ U+30FE are forbidden for `line-break: normal` and `strict` and allowed for `loose`, and the value is conditioned on the content language being Chinese or Japanese. The six move together: there is no value that permits a break before U+3005 alone, which is § B.2 note 14's second method and the treatment § C.3 makes part of its own default level. No value changes the character's class either, because the model has no character classes to change.
disagreements.our_reading: § B.2 note 14 and § C.3 levels 2 and 3 make the subject of the relaxation the single member IDEOGRAPHIC ITERATION MARK 々, not iteration marks (cl-09); only § C.3 level 1 relaxes the class. And § C.2 note 1 makes a relaxed 々 a member of cl-19 against the whole matrix rather than at the line head alone, so the permission and the reclassification are one answer and not two.

cases.quote: § B.2 note 14, third method, worked examples: line end: 国 / line head: 々 <is replaced with> line end: 国 / line head: 国 ; line end: 人 / line head: 々 <is replaced with> line end: 人 / line head: 人 / 行末：国 行頭：々 → 行末：国 行頭：国
cases.rationale: A.9 keys every one of its six members on a single code point; the class holds no ordered pair, unlike the twenty-five paired keys elsewhere in Appendix A. The adjacency that looks like one is this: an iteration mark stands for the character before it, and the specification's own worked example writes that pair as 国 followed by 々. It is two occurrences, and the mark's class is a property of the second occurrence alone rather than of the pair — which is what this case asserts, by asking for the class of item 1 in a stream whose item 0 is the ideograph the mark repeats. An implementation that folds a base character and its iteration mark into one key drops the second item, and one that classifies by the repeated character answers cl-19 for the wrong reason. The overlays are § B.2 note 14's, because the occurrence being classified is the same 々; the third method would rewrite item 1's text to 国 if this occurrence were placed at a line head, which is a mutation of the input and not a class this case can state.

permitted.source: JLReq preferred (A.9; § B.2 note 14, first method)
§ C.2 note 1 and § E.2 note 1: treated as a member of ideographic characters (cl-19) throughout
§ B.2 note 14, third method, which leaves an occurrence that is not at a line head unchanged

cases.quote: A.8 Inseparable characters (cl-08) / 分離禁止文字（cl-08）, table row: 〳 | 3033 | VERTICAL KANA REPEAT MARK UPPER HALF | くの字点上 | used in vertical composition / U+3035 follows this — 縦組で使用 / この文字の後ろにU+3035が配置される. § 3.9.2 lists the class as: Inseparable characters (cl-08) / 分離禁止文字（cl-08）, illustrated —…‥ etc. / —…‥ など
cases.rationale: The boundary the document draws around cl-09. The kana repeat marks (くの字点) are iteration marks by name and by function — the UCS names call them REPEAT MARKs and they repeat the preceding text exactly as A.9's six do — and JLReq nevertheless lists U+3033, U+3034 and U+3035 under inseparable characters (cl-08), not under iteration marks (cl-09). A.9's table has six rows and none of them is one of these three. This case is written because the natural mistake is the generous one: an implementation that assigns a class by reading UCS names, or by asking what a character means, puts these in cl-09 and then applies § 3.1.7's line-start prohibition and § B.2 note 14's relaxations to a key JLReq governs by a different row. Unlike anything in cl-09 these keys carry Remarks, and the Remarks state a writing mode, which is why this case declares vertical composition; the same cell in all six rows of A.9 is empty.

forbidden.why: A.9's table has six rows and U+3033 is not one of them; the document lists this key under A.8 Inseparable characters (cl-08). Membership is what the table says, not what the character's name or its function suggests.

cases.quote: A.8 Inseparable characters (cl-08) / 分離禁止文字（cl-08）, table row: 〵 | 3035 | VERTICAL KANA REPEAT MARK LOWER HALF | くの字点下 | used in vertical composition / 縦組で使用
cases.rationale: The lower half of the same mark, in the same stream, asked separately. The document keys the two halves as two rows of A.8 and states their order in the Remarks of the upper half — `U+3035 follows this` / `この文字の後ろにU+3035が配置される` — rather than as one two-code-point key, so the pair is two occurrences and both are cl-08. That the sequencing is recorded in a Remarks cell and not as a key is the fact worth publishing: an implementation that reads the Remark as a key answers this case with one item where the specification has two, and an implementation that treats the lower half as a combining part of the upper half never asks this question at all. Neither half is a member of cl-09.

forbidden.why: A.9's table has six rows and U+3035 is not one of them; the document lists this key under A.8 Inseparable characters (cl-08).
